key_insight: Research-agent benchmarks can overestimate real-world reliability when they ignore prior session decisions and unfinished workspace state.
engineering_relevance: Evaluate research agents against project history and existing artifacts, not just whether their final deliverables satisfy standalone instructions.
method: Build tasks from real researchers’ agent sessions and full in-progress workspaces.
Replay each workspace to a real request boundary without cleanup, retaining relevant earlier requirements.
Score intent-aligned binary checklists that accept any valid solution.
evidence_signal: Across 75 tasks and seven frontier models, the strongest model passed every checklist item on 66.2% of tasks; three models scoring about 69% on delivery contracts and general norms fell to 28.4–40.0% when contextual requirements were included.
watch_item: The 75-task sample may not capture the full diversity of research workflows, so broader generalization remains uncertain.
paper_title: ARE-bench: Benchmarking Agents' Research Ability in Real-World Researcher Sessions and Workspaces
